title: Helping an Aging Parent | Real Property Planning
description: Find the guidance that fits. Where are you in this journey?

title: My parent is still living independently | Real Property Planning
description: What would you like to plan for next?

title: Staying safe at home | Real Property Planning
description: Most falls happen in the bathroom, on stairs and at the front entry. Simple, low-cost changes like grab bars, brighter lights and clear floors lower the risk…

title: Starting early planning conversations | Real Property Planning
description: Talk early, while nothing is urgent. The goal is to learn what your parent would want, not to change anything today.

title: Home modifications & aging in place | Real Property Planning
description: With the right changes, many parents can stay home longer. Small fixes cost a few hundred dollars; bigger projects like a new shower or a ramp can run…

title: Long-term financial preparation | Real Property Planning
description: Care costs more than most families expect. In Washington, assisted living runs about $7,550 a month, and Medicare does not pay for long-term care.

title: My parent needs more help at home | Real Property Planning
description: What kind of support are you looking into?

title: In-home caregivers & support | Real Property Planning
description: In-home care can cover anything from meals and errands to bathing and nursing visits. In Washington it costs about $45 an hour.

title: Coordinating family caregivers | Real Property Planning
description: When several family members help, a little structure prevents most of the friction: one main contact, one shared calendar and regular check-ins.

title: Safety & home modifications | Real Property Planning
description: When a parent needs help at home, the bathroom and the path to it at night matter most. Small changes are often do-it-yourself; bigger ones need a contractor.

title: Respite & relief options | Real Property Planning
description: Caregivers need breaks to keep going. Respite care covers for you for a few hours or a few weeks, and Washington has a program that can help pay.

title: We're exploring care or housing options | Real Property Planning
description: What are you trying to figure out?

title: What types of senior housing exist? | Real Property Planning
description: Washington has five main kinds of senior housing. The biggest difference between them is how much care is included.

title: How do I compare costs? | Real Property Planning
description: Prices vary widely, and the base rate is rarely the full cost. Compare all-in monthly prices, and ask how they rise as care needs grow.

title: What does my parent qualify for? | Real Property Planning
description: Eligibility depends on two things: how much daily help your parent needs, and their income and assets.

title: How do I have this conversation with my parent? | Real Property Planning
description: Start with what your parent wants, not with your worries. One calm conversation is enough to begin.

title: There's been a health crisis or emergency | Real Property Planning
description: What do you need help with right now?

title: Hospital discharge planning | Real Property Planning
description: Discharge can happen within a day or two. Ask the hospital what care your parent will need next and who arranges it. If it feels too soon, you can ask…

title: Urgent housing or care placement | Real Property Planning
description: When a parent needs a place fast, the hospital social worker is your first call. Adult family homes often have openings when larger places don't.

title: Legal authority to act quickly | Real Property Planning
description: To pay bills or talk with doctors for your parent, you need the right papers. If they aren't signed yet, act now while your parent can still sign.

title: Managing the home during a crisis | Real Property Planning
description: When a parent goes into the hospital or care, the house still needs looking after: locked, bills paid, mail collected. Decisions about selling can wait.

title: My parent's finances and legal documents need attention | Real Property Planning
description: What would you like to address first?

title: Power of attorney & legal documents | Real Property Planning
description: Four documents let family help when it matters: a financial power of attorney, a health care power of attorney, an advance directive and a will. Your parent…

title: Wills & estate planning | Real Property Planning
description: A basic estate plan says who gets what and who's in charge. Beneficiary forms and how the house is titled matter as much as the will.

title: Paying for care | Real Property Planning
description: Most families pay from savings and home equity first. Long-term care insurance, veterans benefits and Apple Health (Medicaid) can help. Medicare does not pay…

title: Property & real estate decisions | Real Property Planning
description: The house is often a parent's biggest asset. Selling, renting and keeping it each have tax and timing effects worth understanding first.
